messages.content: What is the best month to visit Hawaii?

function.name: get_average_monthly_temperature

message.content:
The “best” month to visit Hawaii depends on what you’re looking for—weather, crowds, or price—but most travelers agree that **late spring (April–May) and early fall (September–October)** strike the best balance.

| What you want | Why it’s good |
|---------------|---------------|
| **Great weather** | Average highs 78–84 °F (26–29 °C) with low humidity and minimal rainfall. |
| **Fewer crowds** | These months sit just outside the peak summer (June–August) and holiday (December–January) periods, so resorts and attractions are less crowded. |
| **Better deals** | Hotels and airfare are usually cheaper than in the high‑season months, yet you still get the same sunny beaches and lush scenery. |
| **Wildlife & nature** | Early fall is prime time for whale watching off the coast of Maui and Oʻahu, while late spring offers vibrant flower blooms on the Big Island. |

If you’re a big‑budget traveler who wants the absolute best weather and don’t mind crowds, **June–July** are also excellent—they’re the warmest months (highs 85–88 °F / 29–31 °C) and the ocean is calm for swimming and snorkeling. However, prices and crowds peak during this period.

So, for a blend of pleasant weather, fewer tourists, and reasonable prices, aim for **April, May, September, or October**. If you’re flexible, you can pick any of those months and still have a fantastic Hawaiian getaway.
